question: Which plant hormone is primarily responsible for promoting cell division in fruits and seeds?
options: Auxin
Gibberellin
Cytokinin
Abscisic Acid
explanation: Cytokinins are present in high concentrations in regions of rapid cell division such as developing fruits, seeds, and root tips.

question: The microscopic chemical junction between the axon end of one neuron and the dendrite of the next is called a _______.
options: Synapse
पर्यावरण संतुलन बनाए रखने के उद्देश्य से
विद्यालय की वार्षिक परीक्षा में प्रथम स्थान प्राप्त करने के लिए
गांव के सरपंच द्वारा दिए गए निर्देशों के अनुसार
explanation: At a synapse, electrical impulses trigger the release of chemical neurotransmitters across the synaptic cleft to transmit signals to the next neuron.

question: True or False: Reflex actions are instantly processed and decided by the cerebral cortex of the brain.
options: False
पर्यावरण संतुलन बनाए रखने के उद्देश्य से
विद्यालय की वार्षिक परीक्षा में प्रथम स्थान प्राप्त करने के लिए
गांव के सरपंच द्वारा दिए गए निर्देशों के अनुसार
explanation: Reflex actions bypass the brain's conscious thinking center and are processed directly via reflex arcs in the spinal cord for immediate emergency response.

question: Explain phototropism in plant shoots and how auxin distribution causes shoot bending toward light.
options: Phototropism is directional growth in response to light. When light strikes one side of a shoot tip, auxin diffuses to the shaded side, stimulating cell elongation there and causing the shoot to bend toward the light.
पर्यावरण संतुलन बनाए रखने के उद्देश्य से
विद्यालय की वार्षिक परीक्षा में प्रथम स्थान प्राप्त करने के लिए
गांव के सरपंच द्वारा दिए गए निर्देशों के अनुसार
correct_answer: Phototropism is directional growth in response to light. When light strikes one side of a shoot tip, auxin diffuses to the shaded side, stimulating cell elongation there and causing the shoot to bend toward the light.
explanation: Higher auxin concentration on the shaded side accelerates cell growth relative to the illuminated side, creating unequal growth rates that curve the stem tip toward light.

question: List the major functions of the Forebrain, Cerebellum, and Medulla oblongata.
options: Forebrain (Cerebrum): Thinking, voluntary actions, sensory interpretation, memory. Cerebellum: Controls posture, balance, and precision of movement. Medulla: Controls involuntary actions (blood pressure, salivation, vomiting).
पर्यावरण संतुलन बनाए रखने के उद्देश्य से
विद्यालय की वार्षिक परीक्षा में प्रथम स्थान प्राप्त करने के लिए
गांव के सरपंच द्वारा दिए गए निर्देशों के अनुसार
correct_answer: Forebrain (Cerebrum): Thinking, voluntary actions, sensory interpretation, memory. Cerebellum: Controls posture, balance, and precision of movement. Medulla: Controls involuntary actions (blood pressure, salivation, vomiting).
explanation: The human brain is structurally segregated: cerebrum handles higher cognition; cerebellum maintains equilibrium; medulla manages autonomic brainstem reflexes.

question: Explain the hormonal feedback loop controlling blood glucose levels when a person consumes a sugar-rich meal.
options: High blood glucose after meals is detected by beta cells of the Pancreas, which secrete Insulin hormone into blood. Insulin stimulates cells to absorb glucose and store it as glycogen in the liver. As blood glucose drops back to normal, insulin secretion is reduced.
पर्यावरण संतुलन बनाए रखने के उद्देश्य से
विद्यालय की वार्षिक परीक्षा में प्रथम स्थान प्राप्त करने के लिए
गांव के सरपंच द्वारा दिए गए निर्देशों के अनुसार
correct_answer: High blood glucose after meals is detected by beta cells of the Pancreas, which secrete Insulin hormone into blood. Insulin stimulates cells to absorb glucose and store it as glycogen in the liver. As blood glucose drops back to normal, insulin secretion is reduced.
explanation: Negative feedback loops ensure hormone secretion stays proportional to physiological demand, preventing hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia.
